introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Information and Communication Technologies 2 (0796), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be graded on your ability to use good English, to organize information clearly and to use specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define the term E-Governance and describe one domain or platform of E-Governance in Cameroon (3 marks)

(b) State two reasons why this service is not very much in use in Cameroon. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) E-Governance (3 marks).** E-governance (electronic governance) is the **use of information and communication technologies (the Internet, websites, mobile phones and databases) by the government and its administrations** to deliver services and information to citizens, to businesses and to other government bodies, and to make the administration **more efficient, transparent and accessible**.

**One platform in Cameroon:** the **online tax services of the tax administration (the Directorate General of Taxation)**, where taxpayers register, file their tax returns and pay taxes online instead of queuing at the tax offices. (Other platforms: the single window for foreign trade, GUCE, for import and export formalities; the online registration and results services of the examination boards; online services for passports and visas.)

**(b) Two reasons why it is little used (2 marks)**

1. **Poor and costly Internet access and unreliable electricity**, especially in rural areas, and few citizens own a computer or smartphone.
2. **Low digital literacy and lack of awareness and trust**: many citizens do not know that the services exist or do not know how to use them, and fear fraud or the insecurity of online payment.

(Other accepted answers: lack of trained staff and resistance to change in the administration; weak legal and security framework.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Examples of memories are: ROM, Registers, RAM, EPROM, Cache

(a) Explain the term volatile memory. (2 marks)

(b) Group the above memories into volatile and non-volatile. (2 marks)

(c) State where each of the above memories are located in a PC. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Volatile memory (2 marks).** A volatile memory is a memory that **loses its contents as soon as the power supply is switched off**. It needs a constant supply of electricity to keep its data. Example: RAM.

**(b) Grouping (2 marks)**

| Volatile | Non-volatile |
|---|---|
| RAM, Registers, Cache | ROM, EPROM |

**(c) Location in a PC (2 marks)**

| Memory | Where it is located |
|---|---|
| Registers | **Inside the processor (CPU)** |
| Cache | **Inside or very close to the processor** (levels L1 and L2, and often L3, on the CPU chip) |
| RAM | On the **motherboard**, in the memory (DIMM) slots |
| ROM | On the **motherboard**, in the BIOS/firmware chip |
| EPROM | On the **motherboard or on device and expansion cards**, as a chip that stores firmware and can be erased with ultraviolet light and reprogrammed |

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe three components of an information system. (3 marks)

(b) Discuss TWO factors that determine the reliability of an information system. (2 marks)

(c) Give ONE advantage of an expert system. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Three components of an information system (3 marks)**

1. **Hardware:** the physical equipment used to input, process, store and output data (computers, scanners, printers, servers, network devices).
2. **Software:** the programs that control the hardware and process the data (the operating system and the application programs, such as a database or a spreadsheet).
3. **Data:** the raw facts and figures that are entered and stored (in files and databases) and processed into useful information.

(Further components: **people**, i.e. the users and the technical staff, and the **procedures** or rules for using the system.)

**(b) Two factors that determine reliability (2 marks)**

1. **The quality of the input data**: if the data entered are inaccurate, incomplete or out of date, the information produced is wrong ('garbage in, garbage out'), so data must be validated and verified.
2. **The reliability of the hardware and software, with security, maintenance and back-ups**: well-tested software and equipment that is maintained, protected against viruses and unauthorised access and backed up gives correct results and few breakdowns. (Trained users and a stable power supply also help.)

**(c) One advantage of an expert system (1 mark).** It gives **expert-quality advice quickly, consistently and at any time** (it is available 24 hours a day and does not get tired), and it can keep and share the knowledge of scarce human experts at a lower cost.
